Hi Alice - great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of SLOs you shared
- Target latency: p95 <= 150ms for typical 512-token responses (chat completions).
- Throughput: sustained ~120 reqs/sec peak, with occasional bursts to 200 reqs/sec.
- Concurrency: target ~30 concurrent active sessions.
- Streaming: client expects streaming partial tokens for improved UX (reduce perceived latency).

Primary constraints: SOC2 data handling and per-region hosting (US), cost sensitivity for initial production.

Cost/performance levers we discussed (high level)
- Continuous batching: we can batch short-window requests to improve GPU utilization while honoring streaming via partial-flush thresholds.
- KV/prefix caching: cache repeated prompts or system prompts at the prefix level to avoid re-computation for frequent flows.
- Quantization profiles: int8 or mixed precision profiles available that reduce memory + inference cost (tradeoff: small quality delta).
- Model variants: Redwood-slim-1 (lower cost, lower token throughput) vs Redwood-core-2 (higher quality, higher cost); we can auto-fallback based on latency windows.

Immediate next steps
1) Rishi (cc) will provide a short technical note on streaming + batching tradeoffs and a recommended cache/quant profile for your workload.
2) If helpful, we can run a short benchmark (4999 sample prompts you provide) and return p50/p95 token latencies under your target config.
3) I'll put together a 1M-token ballpark cost for the two model variants and a reserved capacity recommendation.

Attachments: redwood-performance-slo-playbook.pdf (SLO levers & benchmark matrix).

Would you confirm the SLO numbers above and whether you can share a small sample of representative requests (anonymized) for benchmarking? Happy to schedule a 30-min technical session next week.

Thanks,

Hi Alice - quick technical follow-up on streaming and the levers Marissa summarized. High-level answers + recommended baseline config for your SLOs.

1) Streaming + continuous batching
- Continuous batching in our runtime supports partial-flush thresholds. That means: short requests are flushed immediately (configurable at e.g. 8-16 tokens or X ms), and larger requests are batched to optimize GPU utilization.
- For p95 <= 150ms targets for 512-token responses, we recommend a small partial-flush window of 25ms + per-request min tokens flush (to preserve streaming responsiveness). In internal benchmarks this keeps streaming perceived latency within ~10-20ms of no-batching for first chunks while improving overall throughput ~1.6x.

2) Concurrency & throughput sizing
- For your 120 reqs/sec sustained with 30 concurrency, a pair of A100-class GPUs in a dedicated pool with burst capacity should meet baseline needs for Redwood-core-2 with autoscale buffer. If you want a predictable reservation, 2x GPUs with reserved capacity and an autoscale to +1 on burst is a good starting point.

3) Caching strategy
- Prefix caching (system prompts, boilerplate) offers large wins for chat-heavy workloads. Recommend 60s TTL for session-level prefixes, or longer (minutes) if content is shared across sessions. This can reduce redundant transformer compute by ~15-40% depending on overlap.

4) Quantization & model variants
- Recommended profile: Redwood-quant-int8 (mixed int8 weight + fp16 activations) - empirical delta: ~20-30% cost reduction vs fp16 baseline with <2% measured quality delta on our eval set for conversational workloads.
- Fallback plan: use Redwood-slim-1 for non-critical flows and Redwood-core-2 for high-quality generation. We can configure smart routing by latency windows.

5) Benchmark offer
- If Veridian provides 5000 anonymized prompts, we'll run two benchmark runs (slim / core) with streaming enabled and return p50/p95/p99 token latencies, cost per 1M tokens estimate, and detailed config (batch sizes, flush thresholds, quant profile).

I've attached a short CSV with quant profiles and rough perf numbers: quantization-profiles.csv (stub). Happy to jump on a technical call to review results.

Cheers,
